content: To be afraid of death is only another form of thinking that one is wise when one is not; for it is to think that one knows what one does not know.
author: Socrates
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

In Socrates's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: In what area of your life are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action?
